steps.title: Two minutes to the whole idea
steps.body: Ember splits the signal into bands and saturates each one separately. That is the entire concept; everything else is detail. Nothing here changes your settings unless you ask it to.

steps.title: Start from a preset
steps.body: The arrows step through the library. Presets are a faster way to learn what the styles sound like than turning knobs at random.

steps.title: The display is the map
steps.body: Each shaded region is a band. Click one to select it; drag the handles between them to move the crossovers. The band you select is the module that opens below.

steps.title: Drive is the heart of it
steps.body: Drive pushes the band into its style. Watch the display warm up as you turn it — that glow is measured distortion, not level.

steps.title: The style is the character
steps.body: Nineteen of them, grouped by family. Tube is forgiving, tape softens transients, the broken ones are effects rather than colour.

steps.title: Mix is the control you will use most
steps.body: It blends the saturated band back with the clean one. Heavy drive flattens transients; pulling Mix back to 40 percent keeps them and keeps the harmonics.

steps.title: Auto Gain keeps you honest
steps.body: Drive makes things louder, and louder sounds better whether or not it is better. Auto Gain compensates, so you are comparing character rather than volume.

steps.title: A and B
steps.body: Two full snapshots. Set one up, copy it across, change it, and switch between them. Trust this more than your memory of what it sounded like a minute ago.
